chunks: Muhammad ibn Bahr al-Shaybani narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad al-Dhuhli, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Naysaburi narrated to us; he said: Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi' al-Himsi narrated to us; he said: Shu'ayb narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Dhuhli, who said: 'Umara ibn Khuzayma ibn Thabit narrated to me that his uncle narrated to him, and he was among the companions of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family.

The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, purchased a horse from a Bedouin. The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, then hurried in walking to pay him the price of his horse, but the Bedouin delayed. Men began approaching the Bedouin and bargaining with him over the horse, not realizing that the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, had already bought it, until some of them offered the Bedouin more than the agreed price.

So the Bedouin called out and said: 'If you are buying this horse, then buy it; otherwise I will sell it.' When the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, heard the Bedouin, he stood and said: 'Have I not already bought it from you?' People then gathered around the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, and the Bedouin while the two were disputing. The Bedouin said: 'Bring a witness to testify that I have sold it to you.' Whoever came from among the Muslims said to the Bedouin: 'Indeed, the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, would not speak except truthfully.'

Then Khuzayma ibn Thabit came, listened to the exchange between the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, and the Bedouin, and Khuzayma said: 'I bear witness that you have sold it to him.' The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, turned to Khuzayma and said: 'On what basis do you testify?' He said: 'By affirming your truthfulness, O Messenger of Allah.' So the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, made the testimony of Khuzayma ibn Thabit equal to two testimonies and named him Dhū al-Shahādatayn.

key_terms.الْأَعْرَابِيُّ: the Bedouin seller involved in the transaction
key_terms.اِبْتَاعَ: purchased; used here for concluding a sale transaction
key_terms.بِتَصْدِيقِكَ: by affirming your truthfulness; the basis Khuzayma gave for his testimony
key_terms.ثَمَنَ: the price or payment due for the sold item
key_terms.ذَا الشَّهَادَتَيْنِ: the possessor of two testimonies; the title given to Khuzayma
key_terms.شَهَادَةَ: testimony given in establishing the claim
key_terms.شَهِيداً: a witness called to testify to the sale
key_terms.فَرَساً: a horse; the item being bought and disputed

ai.seo_question: How did Khuzayma ibn Thabit come to be called Dhū al-Shahādatayn?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts the Prophet’s purchase of a horse from a Bedouin and the dispute that arose when the seller attempted to deny the completed sale. Khuzayma ibn Thabit testified in support of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, based on his certainty in the Prophet’s truthfulness, and the Prophet granted his testimony the weight of two witnesses. The report is significant in discussions of claims, testimony, and transactional disputes.
